column1: # Proto-Semitic, as reconstructed for roughly 4000 BCE.
# Letters are given phonetic values after Huehnergard and Kogan:
# *š = s, *ś = ɬ, *s = t͡s, *z = d͡z (the sibilants as affricates);
# emphatics as ejectives: *ṭ = tʼ, *ḳ = kʼ, *ṣ = t͡sʼ, *ṣ́ = t͡ɬʼ, *ṯ̣ = θʼ;
# Nouns are stems without case ending or mimation (kalb for *kalbum);
# verbs are suffix-conjugation stems (3rd masculine singular without -a).
# Root-and-pattern morphology is not modelled: each word is a fixed stem.
# Only concepts with a widely accepted reconstruction are listed
# (Huehnergard 2011; Kogan 2011; Militarev & Kogan, SED); the rest are coined.

column2: The reconstructed ancestor of Akkadian, Arabic, Hebrew, Aramaic and Ge'ez: three-consonant roots, ejective emphatics, a lateral fricative, three cases.
Huehnergard, Proto-Semitic Language and Culture (2011); Kogan, Proto-Semitic Lexicon (2011); Militarev & Kogan, Semitic Etymological Dictionary — simplified by hand
